To avoid https://medium.com/nomic-labs-blog/malicious-backdoors-in-ethereum-proxies-62629adf3357[proxy selector clashing], which can potentially be used in an attack, this contract uses the https://blog.openzeppelin.com/the-transparent-proxy-pattern/[transparent proxy pattern]. This pattern implies two things that go hand in hand: 1. If any account other than the admin calls the proxy, the call will be forwarded to the implementation, even if that call matches one of the admin functions exposed by the proxy itself. 2. If the admin calls the proxy, it can access the admin functions, but its calls will never be forwarded to the implementation. If the admin tries to call a function on the implementation it will fail with an error that says "admin cannot fallback to proxy target". These properties mean that the admin account can only be used for admin actions like upgrading the proxy or changing the admin, so it's best if it's a dedicated account that is not used for anything else. This will avoid headaches due to sudden errors when trying to call a function from the proxy implementation. Our recommendation is for the dedicated account to be an instance of the {ProxyAdmin} contract. If set up this way, you should think of the `ProxyAdmin` instance as the real administrative interface of your proxy.

Only its CVXLocker deployment 0x96C68D861aDa016Ed98c30C810879F9df7c64154 is admitted, with current CLeverCVXLocker implementation 0xBfb3A7A5FbB9207dEA82fe06dB4075B8CAEDa534. Current primary CLever app offers lock, unlock and claim future CVX yields, linked official docs retain this exact CVXLocker; October 2026 explorer transactions show deposit, borrow, repay and unlock rather than only recovery. Zero placeholders in the disconnected JavaScript app are not TVL evidence. No CLever USD, deprecated liquidity gauge or retired pool is silently substituted.

deposit(amount) pulls positive caller CVX into the locker, approves and locks it in fixed Convex CVXLockerV2 0x72a19342e8F1838460eBFCCEf09F6585e32db86E for this contract, credits only caller lock ledger, and updates caller rewards/debt first. CVX and clevCVX use 18-decimal base units. CVX remains exposed to Convex lock timing and protocol/contract risks, not immediately liquid shares.

borrow(amount,depositToFurnace) consumes caller accrued rewards first without adding debt; any excess increases caller debt subject to remaining locked CVX * reserveRate >= total debt * 1e9. It mints clevCVX to caller if false; if true it mints to locker then deposits for caller into the configured fixed Furnace. There is no caller target, selector or opaque execution bytes. Furnace is a separately mutable dependency and this boolean path does not admit its external methods or imply immediate CVX redemption.

repay(unusedCVXAmount,clevCVXAmount) ignores the FIRST uint256 in the current implementation; pass zero there. It updates rewards, caps the positive clevCVX amount to caller remaining debt, transfers floor(amount*repayFeePercentage/1e9) clevCVX fee from caller to platform, and burns caller clevCVX via burnFrom. Token allowance to locker and fee funding may be required. It does not repay with CVX despite legacy parameter documentation. Point-in-time repayFeePercentage=0 is not a future fee promise; source maximum is 10%.

unlock(amount) updates caller rewards and matured unlocks, removes only caller lock amount after reserve-rate health check, ceases future reward accrual for pending unlocked amounts and queues CVX across the next available weekly epochs (up to the 17-epoch lock cycle). It is not an immediate withdrawal. withdrawUnlocked() updates maturation and transfers all caller matured unlocked CVX to caller, withdrawing a shortfall from fixed Convex CVX reward pool if needed. Keeper processing of Convex unlocks and actual liquidity remain prerequisites; no date/output guarantee is given.

Accrued rewards are calculated with floor(accRewardPerShareDelta*locked/1e18), first automatically offsetting caller debt. Current reserveRate=500000000 at 1e9 precision, platformFeePercentage=300000000 and harvestBountyPercentage=10000000; these are mutable observations, not immutable economics. Harvesting/zapping/bribe claims, keeper processUnlockableCVX, donation, signatures/verifier, reward-token withdrawals, approvals/target lists and all owner/proxy administration are excluded. No generic zap, arbitrary call or strategy executor is selected.

repay(unusedCVXAmount,clevCVXAmount) ignores the FIRST uint256 in the current implementation; pass zero there. It updates rewards, caps the positive clevCVX amount to caller remaining debt, transfers floor(amount*repayFeePercentage/1e9) clevCVX fee from caller to platform, and burns caller clevCVX via burnFrom. Token allowance to locker and fee funding may be required. It does not repay with CVX despite legacy parameter documentation. Point-in-time repayFeePercentage=0 is not a future fee promise; source maximum is 10%.

unlock(amount) updates caller rewards and matured unlocks, removes only caller lock amount after reserve-rate health check, ceases future reward accrual for pending unlocked amounts and queues CVX across the next available weekly epochs (up to the 17-epoch lock cycle). It is not an immediate withdrawal. withdrawUnlocked() updates maturation and transfers all caller matured unlocked CVX to caller, withdrawing a shortfall from fixed Convex CVX reward pool if needed. Keeper processing of Convex unlocks and actual liquidity remain prerequisites; no date/output guarantee is given.

Accrued rewards are calculated with floor(accRewardPerShareDelta*locked/1e18), first automatically offsetting caller debt. Current reserveRate=500000000 at 1e9 precision, platformFeePercentage=300000000 and harvestBountyPercentage=10000000; these are mutable observations, not immutable economics. Harvesting/zapping/bribe claims, keeper processUnlockableCVX, donation, signatures/verifier, reward-token withdrawals, approvals/target lists and all owner/proxy administration are excluded. No generic zap, arbitrary call or strategy executor is selected.
